sections.title: Basic Concept of Puzzles
sections.content: In puzzle questions, information is given about some persons, places, days, or objects. We have to arrange them correctly based on the given conditions. At Level 1, there are usually 5 to 7 persons or objects, and the solution can be found in 2–3 steps. First, write all names and categories and create a table or a vertical stack.

sections.title: Scheduling Puzzles (Based on Days or Months)
sections.content: In these puzzles, 5–7 people participate in an event on different days (Monday to Sunday) or months. To solve them, create a horizontal table and write the days in order. Fill in direct clues first (such as 'A comes on Monday'). Then apply comparative clues (such as 'B comes after A').

sections.title: Basic Categorization (Department Distribution)
sections.content: Six people are to be distributed into three departments (HR, IT, Marketing), with at least one person in each department. First, create three columns. Fill in the information that is clearly given. If it is stated that 'Ravi is not in HR', then place him in the other two possible options and use the remaining clues to determine the final position.

sections.title: Simple Floor Puzzles
sections.content: Five to six people live on different floors. Consider the ground floor as 1. Create a vertical stack (from 1 to 5 or 6). If it is given that 'A lives on the third floor', write it directly. If it is stated that 'B lives above A', then check the floors above A.

sections.title: Simple Box Puzzles
sections.content: Five to six boxes are placed one above another. Decide the order from top to bottom or bottom to top. If it is given that 'The red box is above the blue box', show this relationship in the stack. At Level 1, there are usually a maximum of 2–3 such relations.

sections.title: How to Perform 2–3 Step Deduction
sections.content: Step 1: Fill in direct information. Step 2: Apply negative information (not, never). Step 3: Use comparisons (above-below, before-after) to fill the empty places. After each step, check the table.

sections.title: Important Strategy
sections.content: 1. Always write the order (days, floors, stack). 2. Read all clues before making assumptions. 3. Fill in only what is certain first. 4. Each person or object will have only one position — do not allow overlap.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Considering the ground floor as 0. 2. Misunderstanding above and below clues. 3. Assigning two positions to the same person. 4. Trying to solve without making a table.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 1 puzzles usually contain 5–7 elements. Creating a table or stack is essential. First apply direct clues, then negative clues, and finally comparison-based clues. The solution is usually found within 2–3 steps.

tricks.title: Build the Structure First
tricks.explanation: Write the complete order of days, floors, or boxes first, then fill in the information.
tricks.example: Write Mon–Tue–Wed–Thu–Fri first, then start filling names.

tricks.title: Fill Direct Information First
tricks.explanation: Immediately fill in the information that is clearly given.
tricks.example: A comes on Wednesday — write A directly under Wednesday.

tricks.title: Use Negative Clues
tricks.example: Ravi is not in HR — place him in IT or Marketing.

tricks.title: Understand Above and Below
tricks.explanation: If B is above A, then B's number will be greater than A's.
tricks.example: A is on the third floor, B is above A — B can be on the fourth or fifth floor.

tricks.title: Before and After Rule
tricks.explanation: If C comes after D, then C's day will be later than D's day.
tricks.example: D is on Monday, C comes after — C will be Tuesday or later.

tricks.title: At Least One Rule
tricks.explanation: If each department must have at least one person, none of them should remain empty.
tricks.example: Ensure at least one name in HR, IT, and Marketing initially.

tricks.title: One Place One Person
tricks.explanation: Only one person can occupy each floor or day.
tricks.example: If A is on the third floor, no one else can be there.

tricks.title: Think from Empty Spots
tricks.explanation: When four positions are filled, the fifth is automatically determined.
tricks.example: In 5 days, if 4 names are filled, the last remaining name goes to the last day.

tricks.title: Combine Two Clues
tricks.explanation: Combine two clues to derive a new conclusion.
tricks.example: A is above B and B is on the third floor — A will be on the fourth or fifth floor.

tricks.title: Final Verification
tricks.explanation: Match the final arrangement with all conditions.
tricks.example: Check that all days are different and no rule is violated.
